note: BUG#20 (qa/bluebook/quality_control.bluebook) — an ACTING (non-creating) command whose only argument is a null `id:` disagreed on refusal kind. Ruby's CommandInterpreter#hydrate_existing falls through `identity_of || identity_from(:id) || identity_from(reference_key) || raise(NotFound, acting_no_identity)`: a null `id:` makes `identity_from` return nil, and with no `subject_kind`/`subject_key` given either, every source comes back empty, so Ruby raises NotFound/acting_no_identity. The compiled Rust conformance binary's generated `extract_id` (registry.rs's own router, called BEFORE kernel::dispatch's already-correct Hydrate::Act NotFound-on-repo.find-miss check is ever reached) let its own `to_id_component` TypeMismatch on `Json::Null` propagate as its final `.ok_or_else` fallback, so Rust refused TypeMismatch where Ruby refused NotFound. Fixed by wrapping `extract_id(facts_json)` at its ONE acting-command call site with a `.map_err` into the exact `RefusalWording.render("NotFound", "acting_no_identity", ...)` wording, computed at codegen time where the command's short name, aggregate name and declared identity reading are in scope. The fixture was written against Compliance's box-surrender review and carried to its generic `Review` (ADR 0143), which has the same shape: a composite identity of two value objects.
